items.title: Section: Where Seeds Truly Reside — The Sautrāntika Doctrine Before the Store-Consciousness, and Suppressing Versus Permanently Destroying Affliction

items.zh: 是故當知，心心所種子隨逐色根，以此為緣，彼得更生。復次，若諸識，非色種子所隨逐者，生無色界異生，從彼壽盡、業盡沒已還生下時，色無種子，應不更生，然必更生。是故當知，諸色種子隨逐於識，以此為緣，色法更生。復次，若諸異生由世間道入初靜慮，若得生彼，爾時欲界諸染污法及餘欲界諸法種子，但被損伏，不能永害。何以故？由此異生從彼定退，欲界染法復現前故；從初靜慮沒已，復還生欲界故。復次，損伏略有三種。一、遠離損伏，二、厭患損伏，三、奢摩他損伏。
items.en:
Therefore one should know: the seeds of mind and mental factors follow the sense faculties, and by taking this as condition, they come to arise again.
Second, following consciousness; first, distinguishing the fault. Furthermore, if consciousness were not followed by seeds of form, an ordinary being born in the formless realm, upon that life-span and karma being exhausted, having died there and returning to be reborn below, would have no seed of form and should not arise again — yet it definitely arises again. Second, concluding it is established. Therefore one should know: the seeds of all forms follow consciousness, and by taking this as condition, form arises again.
Second, distinguishing by person; first, listing the categories; first, ordinary beings; first, distinguishing permanent destruction; first, stating. Furthermore, if an ordinary being enters the first meditative absorption by the mundane path and comes to be born there, at that time the defiled phenomena of the desire realm and the seeds of its remaining phenomena are merely suppressed, not permanently destroyed.
Second, broadly explaining suppression; first, stating and listing. Furthermore, suppression is, in brief, of three kinds: first, suppression through renunciation; second, suppression through aversion; third, suppression through calming meditation.

items.title: Section: Renunciation's Repeated Practice — Dàoxuān's Twenty-Eight Readings, Xuánzàng's Threefold Study — and the Turn to Aversion

items.zh: 云何遠離損伏？謂如有一，棄捨家法，趣於非家，遠離種種受用欲具，受持禁戒。於所受持遠離禁戒，親近、修習、若多修習。由親近、修習、多修習相續不斷故，於諸欲具心不趣入、心不流散、心不安住、心不愛樂，亦不發起彼增上力緣彼境界所起煩惱。如是名為遠離損伏。云何厭患損伏？謂如有一，或由過患想，或由不淨想，或由青瘀等想，或由隨一如理作意，如是如是厭患諸欲。
items.en:
First, suppression through renunciation; first, the question posed. What is suppression through renunciation? Second, the explanation; first, explaining renunciation. There is a person who forsakes household life for homelessness, distancing themselves from every manner of enjoying the implements of desire, and undertakes the precepts. Having undertaken these precepts of renunciation, they draw near to them, cultivate them, and cultivate them repeatedly.
Second, explaining the suppression. Because of this unbroken drawing-near, cultivation, and repeated cultivation, the mind does not enter into the implements of desire, does not scatter towards them, does not abide in them, does not delight in them, nor does it give rise to any affliction arising from that dominant power in dependence on such an object. Third, the conclusion. This is called suppression through renunciation.
Second, suppression through aversion; first, the question posed. What is suppression through aversion? Second, the explanation; first, explaining aversion. There is a person who, whether through the perception of faults, or the perception of impurity, or the perception of bruising and decay, or through some other proper attention, in this or a similar way comes to feel aversion towards the objects of desire.

items.title: Section: Completing Aversion and Calming Meditation — Three Mundane Methods, None of Which Reach the Seed Itself

items.zh: 雖未離欲，然於諸欲修厭逆故，心不趣入，乃至廣說。如是名為厭患損伏。云何奢摩他損伏？謂如有一，由世間道得離欲界欲，或離色界欲。彼由奢摩他任持心相續故，於欲色中心不趣入，乃至廣說。如是名為奢摩他損伏。
items.en:
Though not yet free of desire, because one cultivates revulsion towards the objects of desire, the mind does not enter into them, and so on as before. This is called suppression through aversion.
Third, suppression through calming meditation; first, the question posed. What is suppression through calming meditation? Second, the explanation. There is a person who, through the mundane path, attains freedom from the desire of the desire realm, or from the desire of the form realm. Sustained by the power of calming meditation, the mind does not enter into desire or form, and so on as before. Third, the conclusion. This is called suppression through calming meditation.

items.title: Section: How Noble Ones Permanently Destroy the Seed Itself — The Seven Mental Applications of the Transmundane Path

items.zh: 若聖弟子，由出世道離欲界欲，乃至具得離三界欲，爾時一切三界染污諸法種子皆悉永害。何以故？
items.en: Second, noble ones; first, stating their permanent destruction. If a noble disciple, through the transmundane path, becomes free of the desire of the desire realm, up through complete freedom from the desire of all three realms, at that time all afflictive seeds of the three realms are permanently destroyed outright. Why is this so?

items.zh: 由聖弟子於現法中，不復堪任從離欲退，更起下地煩惱現前；或生上地，亦不堪任從彼沒已還生下地。

items.title: Section: The Sprouting-Seed Simile, the Learner Who Never Falls Back, and the Arhat's Final Extinguishing of Even Wholesome Seeds

items.zh: 如穀麥等諸外種子，安置空逈，或於乾器，雖不生芽，非不種子。若火所損，爾時畢竟不成種子。內法種子損伏、永害，道理亦爾。若聖弟子將入無餘涅槃界時，所有一切善及無記諸法種子皆被損害。由染污法種子滅故，不復能感當來異熟果，亦不復能生自類果。當知是名第四損伏。所謂永害助伴損伏。
items.en:
Just as external seeds such as grain or wheat, when placed in an empty field or a dry vessel, though not sprouting for the time being, remain genuine seeds — yet if damaged by fire, they can never again become seeds at all — the principle of suppression and permanent destruction concerning seeds within one's own being is likewise the same.
Second, arhats beyond further training; first, clarifying their final exhaustion. When a noble disciple is about to enter the realm of nirvāṇa without residue remaining, all their wholesome and neutral seeds alike are rendered incapable of yielding fruit. Because their afflictive seeds have already ceased, they can no longer bring about a future ripened fruit, nor can they any longer generate a further fruit of their own kind.
Second, giving it its distinct name. One should know this is called the fourth kind of suppression, namely the suppression through permanently destroying the accomplice — the afflictive seeds that had helped the wholesome and neutral seeds bear fruit.

items.zh: 復次，具縛者所有心起，若樂俱行、或苦俱行、或不苦不樂俱行，此

items.title: Section: Which Seeds Follow Ordinary Beings, Learners, and Arhats — And the Historic Shift from Scattered Seeds to the Single Store-Consciousness

items.zh: 一切心皆樂種子、苦種子、不苦不樂種子之所隨逐。若起善心、或染污心、或無記心，此一切心皆善種子、染污種子、無記種子之所隨逐。又諸有學不具縛者所有心生，若世間善心、或出世心、或染污心、或無記心，此一切心皆為一切修道所斷煩惱種子之所隨逐。由未斷故，有時得生，亦為所餘諸法種子之所隨逐。又諸無學一切煩惱已永斷者所有心生，若世間善心、若出世心、若無記心，此一切心皆已永離染法種子，但為一切善、無記法種子隨逐相續而生。復次，此所建立種子道理，當知且依未建立阿賴耶識聖教而說。若已建立阿賴耶識，當知略說諸法種子，一切皆依阿賴耶識。又彼諸法若未永斷，若非所斷，隨其所應，所有種子隨逐應知。
items.en:
Second, clarifying its establishment; first, spoken for the śrāvaka vehicle. Furthermore, one should know that this account of the doctrine of seeds just established was given in reliance on teachings not yet establishing the store-consciousness.
Second, spoken for the Mahāyāna; first, revealing their support. Once the store-consciousness has been established, one should know that, in brief, the seeds of all phenomena depend entirely upon the store-consciousness.
Second, distinguishing what follows. Whatever of these phenomena has not yet been permanently severed, or need not be severed at all, their seeds should be understood to follow accordingly.

items.title: Section: Two Kinds of "Falling Back" — Why an Arhat's Meditation May Retreat While the Noble Path Itself Never Does

items.zh: 問：如世尊言：我說阿羅漢苾芻，於四種增上心法現法安樂住中，隨一而退。若彼一切染污種子皆已永害，云何復起下地煩惱？若不復起，彼云何退？答：退有二種。一者、斷退，二者、住退。言斷退者，唯是異生。言住退者，是諸聖者，亦是異生。若世間道斷諸煩惱復起現前，當知爾時斷退故退，亦是住退。若出世道斷煩惱已，心營世務，不專修習如理作意，由此不能於其中間現法樂住數起現前。如先所得，後亦如是。然其下地已斷煩惱不復現前，如是名為住退故退，非是斷退。又若已斷一切煩惱成阿羅漢，而彼一切染法種子未永害者，云何名為心善解脫阿羅漢果諸漏永盡。若已永害，於相續中永無一切染法種子，尚不應起不正思惟，況諸煩惱。是故當知由出世道斷煩惱者，定無有退。
items.en:
Third, resolving the objection; first, raising the scriptural challenge. Question: as the Blessed One said, I declare that an arhat monk falls back from any one of the four exalted mental states of present blissful dwelling. If all their defiled seeds have already been permanently destroyed, how could the affliction of a lower stage arise again? And if it cannot arise again, in what sense do they fall back?
Second, resolving the meaning through the answer; first, stating and listing. Answer: falling back is of two kinds — first, falling back from severance; second, falling back from dwelling.
Second, explaining each; first, falling back from severance: this belongs only to ordinary beings. Second, falling back from dwelling: this belongs to noble ones as well as to ordinary beings.
Fourth, establishing the conclusion; first, showing it in reverse. Furthermore, if one who has severed all afflictions and become an arhat still had defiled seeds not permanently destroyed, how could they be called one whose mind is well liberated, an arhat whose outflows are forever exhausted? Second, establishing it directly. If these have truly been permanently destroyed, then within their mental continuum, wholly free of all defiled seeds, not even improper attention should arise, let alone affliction itself. Therefore one should know that a person who severs affliction through the transmundane path definitely never falls back.

blocks.text: Where are seeds held? The treatise first gives an older answer, then points to the store-consciousness. Then: why worldly meditation only suppresses affliction, while the noble path destroys it.
Seeds of form follow consciousness. Master Cháng Bǎi: form holds seeds of form and mind, and mind likewise. This is the account before the store-consciousness is established.
Master Cháng Bǎi: worldly meditation is like a stone on grass; remove it and the grass grows again.
Master Cháng Bǎi: through precepts one distances oneself from desire; simple provisions cannot arouse greed. What is obtained spoils, and one fears its loss: this is perceiving faults.
Master Cháng Bǎi: up to the preliminary stage is aversion; entering the first absorption is calming. But the seeds of affliction remain uncut.

The seeds are permanently destroyed. Master Cháng Bǎi: the transmundane path cultivates no-self; the mundane rises by revulsion. Of the seven attentions, the penultimate is the uninterrupted path, the last the path of liberation.
Grain kept dry stays seed; burned, it no longer is. Master Cháng Bǎi: undefiled dharmas are pure by nature, hence "not to be severed".

Before the store-consciousness was established, seeds were said to lie in various places; afterwards, all seeds depend on it. Master Cháng Bǎi: hence the *Mahāyānasaṃgraha*'s first chapter is "The Basis of the Knowable".
Master Cháng Bǎi: absorption may be lost, but the path never regresses; the fruit is not lost.
The store-consciousness, proved and described. If you remember one image, keep Master Cháng Bǎi's stone on the grass: meditation can press affliction down, but only insight removes its roots.

quiz.q: When formless beings return below, whence form?
options: seeds of form follow consciousness; each holds the other's seeds
quiz.why: Seeds of form follow consciousness. Master Cháng Bǎi: form holds seeds of form and mind; mind likewise. This is the account before the store-consciousness is established.

quiz.q: What simile does Master Cháng Bǎi use for mere suppression?
options: a stone on grass: remove it and grass grows
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: a stone on grass; remove it and the grass grows again.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain suppression through renunciation?
options: by precepts: ordained, holding the prātimokṣa, provisions can't arouse craving
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: through precepts one distances from desire; simple provisions can't arouse greed.

quiz.q: From what does suppression through aversion come?
options: perceptions of faults, impurity, bruising, or proper attention
quiz.why: From such perceptions. Master Cháng Bǎi: what's obtained spoils, and one fears its loss — this is perceiving faults.

quiz.q: Where does Master Cháng Bǎi set the line between aversion and calming?
options: overcoming hindrances reaches only the preliminary stage; entering the first absorption is calming
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: up to the preliminary stage is aversion; entering the first absorption is calming.

quiz.q: Why can't one leave the three realms even at the highest absorption?
options: the seeds of affliction aren't cut
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the seeds of affliction remain uncut.

quiz.q: What becomes of defiled seeds when a noble disciple is free through the transmundane path?
quiz.why: Permanently destroyed. Master Cháng Bǎi: the transmundane path cultivates no-self; the mundane rises by revulsion.

quiz.q: What are the object and method, and how are the last two attentions assigned?
options: the four truths, seven attentions; the penultimate is the uninterrupted path, the last the path of liberation
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the four truths are the object; of the seven attentions, the penultimate is the uninterrupted path, the last the path of liberation.

quiz.q: Which simile distinguishes suppression and destruction?
options: grain in a dry vessel stays seed; burned, it can never be seed again
quiz.why: Grain kept dry stays seed; burned, it no longer is.

quiz.q: The English says affliction depended on an accomplice. Who is the 助伴 per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: defiled seeds are the helper of wholesome and neutral seeds; the English reverses it
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: defiled seeds help wholesome and neutral seeds bear fruit. The English reverses the direction.

quiz.q: On what basis was the seed doctrine above stated, and what after establishing the store-consciousness?
options: teachings not yet establishing it; once established, all seeds depend on it
quiz.why: Teachings before it was established; afterwards all seeds depend on it. Master Cháng Bǎi: hence the Mahāyānasaṃgraha's first chapter is "The Basis of the Knowable."

quiz.q: The English says "through the seed," which the Chinese lacks. How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain 斷退?
options: affliction was only suppressed, seeds uncut, so it returns; the Chinese has no word "seed"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: affliction was only suppressed, seeds not cut. The Chinese doesn't say "seed."

quiz.q: The Buddha says an arhat falls back from blissful dwelling. From what?
options: absorption, not the noble path, which never regresses
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: absorption is lost, not the path; the path never regresses.

quiz.q: What is the conclusion about one who severs affliction by the transmundane path?
quiz.why: Such a person never falls back. Master Cháng Bǎi: absorption may be lost, the fruit not.

quiz.q: What are phenomena "that need not be severed," and how do seeds follow?
options: transmundane undefiled dharmas, pure by nature; ordinary minds are followed by three kinds of seeds
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: undefiled dharmas are pure by nature, hence "not to be severed"; ordinary minds carry three kinds of seeds.
